basics.name: Kai Ren
basics.summary: Ph.D. student in Intelligence Science and Technology at Kyoto University and research trainee at RIKEN. My research focuses on EMG-based physiological signal modeling, motion intention prediction, and real-time assistive human-machine interaction.

work.position: Research Trainee, Man-Machine Collaboration Research Team
work.summary: Research on EMG-based sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit motion analysis, prediction, and assistive system integration.
highlights: Designed real-time physiological signal processing and neural network pipelines for motion intention prediction.
Built experimental systems for closed-loop control of motorized assistive devices, including chair-based support prototypes.
Developed EMG sensing hardware prototypes, including electrode fabrication, soldering, and acquisition setup.
Conducted data collection, model training, online evaluation, and system-level validation.
